ced.global_kv_source_hidden: encoder layer 19 hidden state feeds decoder Full-Mode global KV (tech report eq. 1)
ced.fact_note: per-token global KV cache 890 bytes (tech report abstract)

csa2.compress_ratios_note: entries 0-39 are backbone layers; 40-42 are the three dspark blocks (SWA-only); verified against config.json text_config.compress_ratios and inference/config.json at the pinned revision: layers 38 and 39 are ratio-1 reuse layers (compressed KV from kv_source 20, topk from index_source 36, compress_rope_theta with YaRN), not SWA-only

indexer.indexer_layer_split: index_source layers 2/8/14/20/24/28/32/36 all own wq_b F8_E4M3 [4096, 1280] + scale [128, 40] and weights_proj BF16 [32, 5120]; wk BF16 [128, 512] + k_norm BF16 [128] exist ONLY on kv_source layers 2/8/14/20 (reference Indexer owns_k: index keys derive from the compressor latent, so only a KV-compressing layer can produce them; every other indexer reads them from that layer's cache) - verified against the pinned model.safetensors.index.json weight_map (24 indexer tensors total)
indexer.indexer_k_projection: projected from the compressor latent on kv_source layers (layers.N.attn.indexer.wk BF16 [128, 512] + k_norm BF16 [128]); non-kv-source indexers reuse those keys from the owning layer's cache

compressor.tensors: layers 2/8/14 (m=2): attn.compressor.wkv BF16 [512, 5120], wgate BF16 [512, 5120], norm BF16 [512]; layer 20 (m=1): wkv + norm ONLY, NO wgate (verified against pinned model.safetensors.index.json weight_map, 11 compressor tensors total)
compressor.semantics_m2: m=2 (layers 2,8,14): pools 2 consecutive tokens into one latent as sum(kv * softmax(score)) with the wgate score; fp32 pooling at runtime (checkpoint bf16); partial-group kv_state/score_state carried across decode steps; a latent is emitted every 2nd token during decode
compressor.semantics_m1: m=1 (layer 20): plain projection norm(wkv(x)) per token, no gate, no pooling, no state (reference Compressor.forward ratio==1 branch)
compressor.semantics_shared: only kv_source_layers own compressors + compressed-KV caches; other layers read the shared cache (Reuse). Latent position mapping: group j takes position j*ratio (first token of its group) and rotates at compress_rope_theta 160000 with YaRN; compressed KV quantized FP4 E2M1 with E4M3 scale per 16 channels AFTER rope; indexer keys quantized separately (FP4, E8M0 per 32)

wq_b_rope_split.layout: wq_b [32768, 1280] is head-major: unflatten(-1, (64 heads, 512 head_dim)); per head dims 0..447 are non-rotated and dims 448..511 are the rope tail
wq_b_rope_split.rope: rope applied ONLY to the tail 64 dims with adjacent element pairs as complex numbers. RESOLVED against the pinned reference (session 7): layer 0 (compress_ratio 0) uses PURE theta 10000, no YaRN; every CSA2 layer (compress_ratio > 0) builds ONE YaRN table (base compress_rope_theta 160000, factor 16, original_seq_len 65536, beta 32/1) and uses it for ALL rotations - q, window kv, compressed kv, indexer q AND indexer k (the indexer inherits the attention's freqs_cis). The earlier 'yarn theta 10000 factor 16' claim is not what the reference computes for any layer
wq_b_rope_split.source: reference Attention.__init__ freqs_cis branch + Indexer.forward at pinned revision

kv_cache.global_kv_codec: MXFP4-class E2M1, one E4M3 scale per 16 channels, NO second-level global scale, quantized AFTER rope

hyper_connection.scheme: Single-Pass mHC (tech report 2.4.1), deployment kernel Mega-mHC
hyper_connection.coefficient_layout: Pinned from kernel.py hc_split_sinkhorn_kernel: mixes [24] = fn.x_normed (fp32); pre[j] = sigmoid(mixes[j]*scale[0] + base[j]) + eps; post[j] = 2*sigmoid(mixes[4+j]*scale[1] + base[4+j]) (NO eps); comb[j][k] = mixes[8 + j*4 + k]*scale[2] + base[8 + j*4 + k]; comb = row_softmax(comb) + eps, then col-norm/(sum+eps), then (sinkhorn_iters-1) x (row-norm, col-norm), every denominator + eps. Sinkhorn order verified identical to the glm5-dsa lane oracle (independent corroboration)

engram.residency: operator ruling 2026-09-11: row-shard both tables across the 16 mesh ranks of TP8xPP2 via weightd lazy attach + mesh broadcast (engram_row_shard); no host-resident table and no all_reduce gather

hash_addressing_resolved.token_map: token ids mapped through a 99092-entry compressed vocab (normalization-collapsed: NFKC/NFD/strip/lowercase); map size is asserted == engram_compressed_vocab_size
hash_addressing_resolved.hash: per position: last up-to-4 tokens (lookback stops at sequence start and DEAD/image tokens, pad-filled); per (layer, lookback) odd multiplier from RNG seed 10007*layer_id bounded by int64/compressed_vocab; rolling XOR across lookbacks; id = (rolling % prime) + offset
hash_addressing_resolved.primes: disjoint prime bucket ranges per (layer, ngram 2..4, head 0..7), drawn in order starting from engram_vocab_size-1 = 15999999; 24 ids per layer per token ((4-1) orders x 8 heads)
hash_addressing_resolved.decode_read: per decode step per engram layer: 24 row gathers of 256B fp8 E4M3 + 8B E8M0 scales (~6.3KB) -> dequant bf16 -> wkv Linear(6144 -> 5120*(hc_mult+1)=25600) -> split key[4,5120]+value[5120] -> normalized-dot sigmoid sqrt-gate per hc copy -> residual add

embed_table_bytes_measured.note: sha256-verified shard headers at dba1be0a; each engram module fills warm shard model-00047/00048 (~101.5 GiB incl its small wkv/q_weight/k_weight tensors); replaces the earlier 98385580032 estimate

engram_row_shard.status: OPERATOR-RULED 2026-09-11 (TP8xPP2, 16 mesh ranks, one rank per spark): row-shard, 12.3GiB/spark; implementation contract below
engram_row_shard.partition: reference ParallelEngramEmbedding layout exactly: rows_per_rank = ceil(entries/16) (layer1 384006168 -> 24000386, rank15 holds 24000378; layer14 384016682 -> 24001043, rank15 holds 24001037); owner(rank) = id // rows_per_rank; local_row = id - owner*rows_per_rank; ids are in-range by hash construction but the access path fail-closes SPARK_STATUS_SCHEMA_ERROR on id >= entries (table/hash mismatch)
engram_row_shard.shard_file: ONE stagepack-wire-format file per rank (engram shard pack, own tensor-kind space + own contract sha, NOT the GPU stagepack kinds): rank slice of layers.1 and layers.14 embed.weight F8_E4M3 [rows_r, 256] + embed.scale F8_E8M0 [rows_r, 8], plus replicated per layer: wkv.weight F8_E4M3 [25600, 6144] + scale E8M0 [800, 192], q_weight/k_weight BF16 [4, 5120]; file naming <arm>.engram.rank<h> (sparkdata tree), .experts manifest with row-block expert entries (32768-row blocks; <=733 blocks/table/rank, payload 8MiB << SPARK_WEIGHTD_EXPERT_BYTES_MAX)
engram_row_shard.access_path: per decode step per engram layer: (1) compressed token map (99092, sha-pinned) -> rolling XOR hash (pinned: multipliers seed 10007*layer_id odd, per-(order,head) prime % from 15999999 drawn in order) -> 24 ids; (2) owner = id // rows_per_rank; (3) OWNED columns: weightd lazy-attach #2 on the rank's shard file, row-block Ensure/lease (expert-pool pattern), row bytes read from the leased GPU map; (4) REMOTE columns: owner's driver memcpy's the 264B row (256B fp8 + 8B E8M0 scale) into its mesh slot at the deterministic staging offset col*264 + layer*6336 and MeshBroadcasts to the 15 peers, arrival signalled by the existing per-offset seq doorbell; (5) consumer polls all 24 seq offsets (deadline -> SPARK_STATUS_BUSY fail-closed, never zero-fill), assembles [24,256]+[24,8]; (6) dequant bf16 exactly as reference (float().unflatten(-1,(-1,32))*scale.float().unsqueeze(-1) -> bf16) then reference Engram block (wkv, split key[4,5120]+value[5120], normalized-dot sigmoid sqrt-gate, residual add); wkv/q_weight/k_weight read via the same shard lease (replicated)
engram_row_shard.primitive_audit: NO new weightd primitive required: second lazy attach is allowed (SPARK_WEIGHTD_ATTACHES_PER_CONNECTION_MAX 8), row-block Ensure/Acquire/lease is the proven expert-pool path, and the cross-rank fetch is SparkWeightdClientMeshBroadcast (proven by the hidden-transport ring); 24 cols x 264B x 2 layers = 12,672B/step staged, trivial vs the 16MiB mesh slot
engram_row_shard.fail_closed: unresolvable access fail-closed at SPARK_FAIL, no zero-row fabrication, no direct file reads in driver code (WEIGHTS LAW): shard bytes reach the driver only through weightd leases/maps; oracle/anchor and shard tooling are exempt tooling
engram_row_shard.cut_and_verify: tools/dsv41_flash_engram_shard.py cut mode (sparkcap on the node, chunked per source shard) + verify mode: headers==index, byte-verify vs checkpoint, per-rank boundary ranks (0, mid, last-row), sha256 per shard, .experts census; ladder synth first, real-row pieces on rank0 shard after cut

dspark.sidecar: MTP-sidecar law: separate sysadmin sidecar files, ported LAST

precision.dense_linear_codec: FP8 E4M3 with UE8M0 scale, 32x32 weight blocks (quantization_config.weight_block_size, scale_fmt ue8m0)
precision.expert_codec: packed FP4 stored as I8 (2 nibbles/byte), UE8M0 scale per 32 input elements per output row
precision.qk_norm: q_norm BF16 [1280] on q_lora, kv_norm BF16 [512] on kv latent
precision.attention_window_kv_runtime: act_quant inplace semantics: window-KV cache rows are bf16 of the fp8 round trip (per-32-channel ue8m0 scale = 2^ceil(log2(amax/448)), amax floored 1e-4, clamp +/-448); attention denominators add exp(sink - max) per head with no sink value term

tp_divisibility.resolved_o_groups: reference implementation (inference/model.py Attention.__init__) computes n_local_groups = o_groups // world_size and requires it >= 1: the o-path is reference-faithful only for TP in {1,2,4,8}. wo_a is block-diagonal per group (einsum over n_local_groups x [o_lora_rank, heads_per_group*head_dim]); wo_b is RowParallel over n_groups*o_lora_rank. TP16 (8 % 16 != 0) has NO reference-supported o-path; an exemption would need a half-group split with pairwise partial-sum reduction that does not exist in the reference code. Topology decision (TP16 exemption design vs TP4xPP4/TP8 fallback) is an operator/architecture call, escalated in PR #914

topology.unsupported: TP16: 8 o_groups cannot split across 16 ranks in the reference o-path
topology.serving: TP8xPP2 on 16 Sparks: world size 16 equals the engram row-shard mesh; TP8 alone needs an 8-rank engram cut that does not exist
topology.hill_climb: TP4xPP4 and TP2xPP8 are reference-supported and must be measured before a topology is fixed
